newsitem.title: USA: CKE to buy Hardee's fast food chain from Imasco.
newsitem.headline: CKE to buy Hardee's fast food chain from Imasco.

text.p: CKE Restaurants Inc., known for its Carl's Jr. fast food restaurants, Monday announced plans to acquire the troubled Hardee's chain, from Imasco Ltd. for about $327 million.
Anaheim, Calif.-based CKE said it will pay about $327 million for the 788 company-operated Hardee's and 2,364 franchised Hardee's restaurants, giving Carl's Jr. a national presence.

Hardee's has restaurants in 40 states, mainly in the southeast and midwest United States, as well as in 10 other countries. Hardee's is ranked either No. 1 or No. 2 by market share in half of the markets in which it operates.
More than 550 of Carl's Jr.'s 676 restaurants are located in California where it ranks No. 2 in most of the state.
"Our chairman is very growth oriented and feels very strongly that the Carl's Jr. brand can become a much larger company and brand," CKE spokesman Loren Pannier said.

"We have established a precedent for fixing other troubled brands ... (this) was a strategic opportunity to give Carl's Jr. a chance to become a national brand without trying to open (restaurants) market by market," Pannier said.
Pannier said the acquisition would boost CKE's earnings in the current fiscal year and there would be "selective store closures" of Hardee's restaurants.

The deal is the most aggressive yet by CKE, which has expanded its Carl's Jr. franchise by acquiring troubled restauants. CKE has bought Summit Family Restaurants and Casa Bonita and made investments in both Rally's and Checkers.

CKE has also boosted the Carl's Jr. brand with a series of high profile television adverts that featured celebrities such as basketball star Dennis Rodman. Same store sales rose 10.7 percent last year.

Hardee's has been losing money recently and has reported negative same store sales for a number of quarters. In April Hardee's Montreal-based parent Imasco said the chain lost C$11 million in the first quarter.

"This is a strong marriage of two well-known brands," said William Foley II, CKE's chairman and chief executive officer. "Teaming Carl's Jr.'s big, juicy charbroiled burgers with Hardee's superior breakfasts enables us to showcase each chain's strengths," he said.

Hardee's has about 30 percent of its sales during breakfast, the highest in the quick-service segment. For the last fiscal year, Hardee's restaurant sales were $2.98 billion while CKE Restaurants' were $742 million.

CKE said it will start by dual branding Hardee's with Carl's Jr. restaurants in two test markets offering Hardee's breakfast and Carl's Jr. lunch and dinner menus. During the test period the rest of the Hardee's system will offer new products based upon Carl's Jr. menu.

CKE said it will pay for the acquisition by issuing about $100 million of CKE common stock and giving a $50 million note to Imasco that may be converted into CKE stock. The balance will be funded through a bank loan.
CKE said it expects significant operating synergies, including enhanced marketing and media buying power, leveraged purchasing power, and reduced costs.

CKE Restaurants and its subsidiaries operate a total of 928 restaurants under several brands including Carl's Jr., Rally's, Carl's Jr./Green Burrito, Taco Bueno, JB's Restaurants as well as HomeTown Buffet restaurants and Galaxy Diner restaurants.
